title: Fix network panel Forget centering, add Cancel for in-flight connects

workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The cancellation gate drops a saved-network connect while Quickshell's asynchronous PSK update can still activate it
leads.consequence: For a saved PSK profile when the user supplies new credentials, Quickshell first issues Settings.Update and activates only in its later D-Bus completion callback. If Cancel arrives before that callback, the Wi-Fi device is still Disconnected or still Connected to the previous network, so this PR skips Device.Disconnect and clears its local action. The pending callback subsequently requests activation anyway; the supposedly cancelled Wi-Fi connection can replace the existing connection. The test mock incorrectly changes the device state synchronously in connectWithPsk. This is a source-established race, not a hardware reproduction.
leads.triage: folded into optional note (pre-activation Cancel UI-only); corroborates Opus residual

leads.summary: Manual connection activation does not clear NetworkManager's device autoconnect block
leads.consequence: Successful Device.Disconnect sets MANUAL_DISCONNECT. NetworkManager 1.58.1 checks the blocked flags for automatic activation; explicit network activation is permitted but does not unset that flag. Thus the panel can manually reconnect once, but after that connection drops it will not auto-reconnect as the comment promises. The only core clear of all blocked flags found is the device's Autoconnect=true D-Bus setter, which this panel does not call. Toggling the radio uses Networking.wifiEnabled, not that setter. Consider restoring device autoconnect deliberately with a user-visible policy, or document that Cancel suspends auto-reconnect until reset.
leads.triage: refuted: NM 1.58.1 nm-device.h L695,L703-704 INTERNAL includes MANUAL_DISCONNECT; nm-device.c L18046-18047 unsets it on PREPARE..ACTIVATED

leads.summary: Clearing keyboard focus does not disarm the mouse Cancel-to-Forget transition
leads.consequence: Cancel sets wifiActionFocused=false but the right-edge MouseArea still enables itself when the saved row is no longer busy and still known. Its next onClicked takes the unconditional non-Cancel branch to forget(row.net), irrespective of wifiActionFocused. If a second click is delivered to the same right-edge slot, including a physical double-click when the row remains under the pointer, it deletes the saved profile. Qt 6.11 emits clicked for both clicks when no doubleClicked handler is connected. Scans can rebuild delegates and reactivate hover as well. A real second mouse activation, not just a boolean focus check, belongs in the regression test.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Finding A); corroboration

leads.summary: Device-level cancel can stop an unrelated activation because the gate tests only the device state
leads.consequence: If another client is activating a different SSID on the selected Wi-Fi device while this panel has an in-flight connect action (for example its own request is still pending), device.state=Connecting passes isActivationPending regardless of which connection owns that device state. Cancel then issues NM Device.Disconnect for the other activation and clears the panel action, while the panel's delayed request can still activate later. The mock has no competing activation and directly sets state=Connecting for the tracked request. This is a conditional source-level race, not reproduced with an external NM client.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N-a); optional note

leads.summary: TERM cleanup waits for any foreground enterprise add or edit command to finish
leads.consequence: Only the final nmcli connection up is backgrounded. Bash defers the TERM trap while it waits for a foreground nmcli connection add or a connection edit pipeline, so the UI immediately stops tracking but a blocked nmcli child can continue changing the profile and cleanup occurs only when it returns. In a sandboxed 2-second add stand-in, deletion had not happened 0.2s after TERM; deletion occurred when add returned and bash exited 143. The delay can be longer if NM or its polkit authorization stalls. Cancel needs lifecycle-safe cleanup of all blocking stages and a way to prevent a retry while the previous helper still exits.
leads.triage: no defect: deferred trap then cleanup, matches Opus trap probe

leads.summary: The behavioral fixture never operates the Cancel control or models delayed NetworkManager state
leads.consequence: The claimed prompt-keyboard test calls panel.activateSelected() directly, not the visible cancelPwBtn or any Enter/Escape event. The mock makes every connect synchronously set device.state=Connecting, unlike the real asynchronous connection request and PSK-update path. Its forget() only increments a counter and never flips known or stateChanging, so the fixture also cannot prove the forget lane completes. A mutant that adds `enabled: false` to cancelPwBtn still passes all 126 network-test.sh assertions in the isolated run, and all direct-call fixture assertions remain unaffected by that UI change; keyboard and mouse Cancel are disabled. Add actual focused key/mouse delivery, delayed activation and a simulated NM forget completion.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (R1-N3 partial); Details bullet

leads.summary: Open PR #13680 separately implements the same Cancel slot and conflicts with this PR
leads.consequence: #13680 independently adds cancelConnect(), a second Cancel prompt control, and its own Enter and right-edge slot wiring. GitHub reports its head MERGEABLE against its base e332dc9, not necessarily against this head. A three-way merge using #13680's own base has 12 conflict regions in Panel.qml and one in network-test.sh, and applying its diff to this head rejected 8 of 9 network panel hunks. Choosing #13680's profile-level network.disconnect() implementation during resolution would reintroduce a no-op while connecting; both PRs cannot be merged without integrating their competing controls and tests.
leads.triage: verified by gh: #13680 open, cancelConnect() uses network.disconnect(); optional note

leads.summary: Enterprise reuse PR #12889 requires ownership-aware cancellation cleanup at merge time
leads.consequence: #12889 intentionally reuses existing enterprise profiles and deletes only a profile it just created on failure. This PR's TERM drop() deletes its UUID unconditionally. A three-way merge of Model.js at #12889's base conflicts at the entire enterprise helper; keeping only this PR loses reuse, keeping only #12889 loses cancellation cleanup, and combining an unconditional drop with reused UUIDs would erase an institutional profile on Cancel. The resolution must distinguish newly created from reused profiles before deletion and test both cancellation cases.
leads.triage: verified by gh diff: #12889 deletes only when created; optional note

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** At `c24d590c`, double-clicking a saved row's Cancel forgets it.

[Earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13088#issuecomment-5826199588), after the [reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13088#issuecomment-5860031189):
- Resolved: Cancel reaching NetworkManager, Esc in the prompt, enterprise cleanup, pending-Forget connect, `cancelledSsid`.
- Partly: tests. Still present (pointer only): armed Forget after Cancel.

### Double-click on Cancel runs Forget

Clearing `wifiActionFocused` fixes Enter, but the slot's MouseArea never reads it: after the first click cancels, the second click of a double-click runs `forget()`. The earlier fix idea was incomplete. **Impact:** the saved profile and credentials are deleted without confirmation.

**Suggested change:** add `onDoubleClicked: {}` to the slot's `rightMouse` MouseArea (tested below) and a fixture double-click step.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at c24d590c)</summary>

# Reproducer: R1-F2 (pointer path) - a double-click on a saved row's Cancel forgets the network

Save as `cancel-dblclick-repro.sh` and run it with the path of an Omarchy checkout at the PR head:

```bash
bash cancel-dblclick-repro.sh /path/to/omarchy
```

It runs the real `shell/plugins/panels/network/Panel.qml` against the PR's own `test/shell.d/fixtures/network-cancel/mocks/NetworkMock.qml` (same singleton swap as `network-cancel-test.sh`), on Qt's offscreen platform. Two substitutions: `shell/Ui/KeyboardPanel.qml` (a layer-shell PanelWindow) is replaced by a plain Item so no compositor is needed, and `omarchy-dns`, `omarchy-network-band` and `omarchy-network-status` are no-op stand-ins (the PR's test stubs the first two the same way). Pointer events are real Qt events sent with QtTest's `TestEvent` (`mouseDoubleClickSequence` = press, release, press, double-click, release, 60 ms apart). `Cafe WiFi` is a saved (known) network in the mock.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Double-click on a saved row's Cancel slot: the second click forgets the
# network. Usage: cancel-dblclick-repro.sh /path/to/omarchy-checkout
# Runs the real Panel.qml with the PR's NetworkMock, on Qt's offscreen platform.
# The layer-shell KeyboardPanel is replaced by a plain Item so no compositor is
# needed; everything else (rows, slot MouseArea, cancel/forget logic) is real.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT=$(cd -- "$1" && pwd)
stage=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf -- "$stage"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$stage/network" "$stage/bin" "$stage/home"
cp -r "$ROOT/shell/Ui" "$stage/Ui"
ln -s "$ROOT/shell/Commons" "$stage/Commons"
cp -r "$ROOT/test/shell.d/fixtures/network-cancel/mocks" "$stage/mocks"
cp "$ROOT/shell/plugins/panels/network/Model.js" "$stage/network/"
sed -e 's|^import Quickshell.Networking$|import Quickshell.Networking\nimport "../mocks"|' \
    -e 's/\bNetworking\./NetworkMock./g' \
    "$ROOT/shell/plugins/panels/network/Panel.qml" >"$stage/network/Panel.qml"
cat >"$stage/Ui/KeyboardPanel.qml" <<'QML'
import QtQuick
Item {
  id: root
  required property Item anchorItem
  required property QtObject bar
  property var owner: null
  property int contentWidth: 380
  property int contentHeight: 200
  property bool open: false
  property Item focusTarget: null
  default property alias contentItem: holder.children
  function fittedContentWidth(w) { return w }
  function fittedContentHeight(h) { return h }
  visible: open; width: contentWidth; height: contentHeight
  Item { id: holder; anchors.fill: parent }
}
QML
cat >"$stage/shell.qml" <<'QML'
import QtQuick
import QtTest
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Networking
import qs.Commons
import "mocks"
import "network" as Network
ShellRoot {
  Window {
    id: win; visible: true; width: 720; height: 1400
    Network.Panel {
      id: panel
      bar: QtObject {
        property color foreground: Color.foreground
        property color barForeground: Color.foreground
        property color urgent: Color.urgent
        property string fontFamily: Style.font.family
        property string position: "top"
        property int barSize: 24
      }
    }
  }
  TestEvent { id: ev }
  function slot() {  // the right-edge slot of the row that is connecting
    function walk(it) {
      if (it.text === "󰅖" && it.visible && it.parent.focusable === undefined) return it.parent
      for (var i = 0; i < it.children.length; i++) { var r = walk(it.children[i]); if (r) return r }
      return null
    }
    return walk(win.contentItem)
  }
  property int step: 0
  property bool dbl: true
  Timer {
    interval: 400; repeat: true; running: true
    onTriggered: {
      if (step === 0) { panel.open() }
      else if (step === 1 || step === 4) {
        NetworkMock.cafe.forgets = 0; NetworkMock.device.disconnects = 0
        panel.forgetActive = false; panel.forgetSsid = ""
        panel.connectDirectly("Cafe WiFi")      // Cafe WiFi is a saved network
      } else if (step === 2 || step === 5) {
        var s = slot()
        ev.mouseMove(s, s.width / 2, s.height / 2, -1, Qt.NoButton, Qt.NoModifier)
        if (dbl) ev.mouseDoubleClickSequence(s, s.width / 2, s.height / 2, Qt.LeftButton, Qt.NoModifier, 60)
        else ev.mouseClick(s, s.width / 2, s.height / 2, Qt.LeftButton, Qt.NoModifier, -1)
      } else if (step === 3 || step === 6) {
        console.log((dbl ? "double-click" : "single click") + " on Cancel: cancelled=" +
          (NetworkMock.device.disconnects === 1 && panel.actionKind === "") +
          " forget() calls=" + NetworkMock.cafe.forgets + " row status=" + (panel.forgetSsid === "Cafe WiFi" ? "Forgetting" : "idle"))
        if (step === 3) dbl = false; else Qt.quit()
      }
      step++
    }
  }
}
QML
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$stage/bin/noop"; chmod +x "$stage/bin/noop"
for c in omarchy-dns omarchy-network-band omarchy-network-status; do ln -s noop "$stage/bin/$c"; done
HOME="$stage/home" PATH="$stage/bin:$PATH" QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software \
  timeout 30 quickshell -p "$stage" --no-color 2>&1 | grep -E 'on Cancel:' | sed 's/^ DEBUG qml: //'
```

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Tests: the prompt Cancel and the enterprise trap are covered only by source regexes. The fixture check "cancel disarms the slot so a second click cannot land on Forget" never arms the slot first, so it also passes at `989451c4`.
- Two separate clicks 400 ms apart also forget. By source, the slot shows Forget before the second click there, so that case is closer to intent.

**Verified**
- `wifiDevice.disconnect()` gated on the device being Connecting reaches `Device.Disconnect` (Quickshell 0.3.1 and master, NetworkManager 1.58.1). With the device Connected or Disconnecting, nothing is torn down.
- The `MANUAL_DISCONNECT` autoconnect block is cleared when the device next enters PREPARE through ACTIVATED, so activating any network clears it, as the code comment says. Otherwise it persists (for example across suspend or a Wi-Fi off/on), so a cancelled switch stays offline until a network is picked.
- The prompt Cancel takes focus while connecting. Esc and Enter on it abort, and a second Esc closes the prompt (real key events, offscreen Qt).
- The enterprise TERM trap kills a running `connection up`, deletes the profile and exits 143. During `connection add` or `edit` it waits for that step, then deletes.
- The new fixture gives 24 PASS at `c24d590c` and the same 6 FAIL at `989451c4` that the author reported. `network-test.sh`: 126 ok.

**Optional notes**
- `isActivationPending()` checks the whole device, not the tracked SSID. A Cancel before the device reports it is activating (during the PSK settings update, or while NetworkManager tears down the current network for the new one) is UI-only, and one landing while another SSID is activating aborts that one instead. Both windows are narrow and were not measured.
- Open #13680 adds its own Cancel to the same `Panel.qml` code using the profile-level `network.disconnect()`, the path that does not work while connecting. Open #12889 rewrites the same enterprise helper and only deletes profiles it created, so combining it with this TERM trap needs the same ownership check.
</details>
